title: Learned spatial expression mode associates with treatment response in a small cohort
summary: An unsupervised spatial-learning model fitted 20 expression modes in pretreatment samples from 21 cutaneous squamous-cell-cancer patients. A subsequently selected mode showed greater neighboring-cell contrast in responders than non-responders. This is an exploratory same-cohort spatial association, not an independently validated treatment-response predictor.
ai_technology: SAIL; unsupervised sparse spatial projection learning

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, computational objectiveIII-C, clinical applicationV-D and statistical limitations; no operational laboratory protocols

evidence.tested: Spatial modes were fitted without response labels from 28 pretreatment biopsies in 21 patients. Response comparisons subsequently selected the most discriminative of 20 modes.
evidence.unknown: Post-training mode selection uses the same 21 response labels. Nominal comparisons across 20 modes do not establish multiplicity-adjusted confirmation or held-out predictive accuracy. Prior work already linked spatial organization to response; this refinement does not establish a causal immune mechanism or treatment benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Learned sparse projections optimize spatial coherence rather than simply plotting coordinates. The resulting mode supplies the patient-level contrast examined against recorded response.
